title: ProfiliTable: Profiling-Driven Tabular Data Processing via Agentic Workflows

problem.claim: Table processing tasks are foundational but error-prone in real-world data pipelines.

gap.claim: Existing LLM-based approaches struggle with ambiguous instructions, complex task structures, and insufficient structured feedback, producing code that may be syntactically correct but semantically flawed.

contributions.claim: ProfiliTable is an autonomous multi-agent framework centered on dynamic profiling for iterative table-processing workflows.
The framework combines profiling-based exploration, curated-operator retrieval for code synthesis, and execution-feedback-driven refinement.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on a diverse benchmark covering 18 tabular task types report that ProfiliTable consistently outperforms strong baselines.
The reported advantage is particularly pronounced in complex multi-step scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Table processing is important but error-prone.
LLM-based automation can fail under ambiguity, structural complexity, and limited feedback.
ProfiliTable addresses these challenges through dynamic profiling and iterative multi-agent refinement.
The authors report improvements over strong baselines across 18 tabular task types, especially for complex multi-step tasks.
The results are presented as supporting dynamic profiling for translating ambiguous intents into robust, governance-compliant transformations.

source_observation.claim: Dynamic profiling is used to construct and refine a unified execution context through exploration, synthesis, and feedback.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly grounding generation in observed data state and iterative diagnostics may reduce semantic errors from ambiguous instructions.

application.claim: For complex data transformations, use profiling and execution feedback as part of a closed-loop workflow rather than relying on one-shot code generation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this workflow is superior for tasks outside the reported tabular benchmark or for all transformation settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, baseline methods, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe implementation details, resource requirements, failure cases, or reproducibility materials.
